jobs.occupation: Technical assistant (m/f/d) (16/2026) (Biologisch-technische/r Assistent/in)
jobs.description: Your area of responsibility Research topic: Plant immunity Plant pathogens secrete small molecules in their host to manipulate cellular processes and cause disease. Plants are not defenseless, however, and have evolved a wide variety of immune receptors to sense these pathogen-associated molecules and subsequently trigger an immune response to restrict pathogen infection. In the Molecular Plant Immunity research group, we investigate the molecular basis of effector recognition and immune receptor activation, and how evolutionary forces shape these processes. We then leverage this knowledge to develop strategies for sustainable disease resistance in crops. Your tasks:• Independent execution of molecular biology laboratory tasks• Microbiological work with bacteria and fungi under sterile conditions• Organization and maintenance of standardized workflows in the laboratory• Plant husbandry• Support lab members in their experiments• Documenting experimental procedures and resultsYour profile• Completed training as a Biological technical assistant or equivalent• Independent and solution-oriented work ethic• Enthusiasm for teamwork• Ability to work in a multi-cultural, multi-ethnic environment with sensitivity and respect for diversity• Desirable knowledge and skills include:• Good English language skills (written and spoken)• Experience in microbiology and molecular biology work• Experience in handling biosafety S1 organismsPlease apply with a cover letter and your CV containing the contact details of two referees and by the 7th of December 2026. If you have any questions, please contact Clemence Marchal (clemence.marchal@ipb-halle.de).We offer• Modern Working Conditions: Comprehensive introduction to work techniques and a modern research environment with state-of-the-art equipment and up-to-date software• Career Development: Targeted training opportunities and access to a specialized library with electronic resources and quiet workspaces• Compensation & Security: Classification according to TV-L including annual bonus, pension scheme (VBL), health offers, and discounted canteen meals• Ideal Working Environment: A varied and inspiring workplace in an international setting at a leading scientific and innovation hub• Team Spirit and Leadership Culture: An open culture that strengthens teamwork, enables career networking, and promotes your research skills.• Work-Life Balance: Flexible working models, remote work options, and 30 days of annual leave – for a balanced work-life experience.About us The Leibniz Institute of Plant Biochemistry (IPB) is a non-university research institution of the Leibniz Association on the Weinberg Campus of the Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg. As a foundation under public law, the IPB is under direct supervision of the state of Saxony-Anhalt.The IPB is an internationally recognized research institution and consists of four scientific Departments, additional independent junior research groups, and the Department Administration & Infrastructure (about 200 employees, including about 40 PhD students). Research at the IPB aims to understand the (bio)chemical basis of plant resilience and performance in challenging environments related to climate change. The IPB offers excellent research facilities and state-of-the-art infrastructure to investigate the chemical diversity, biochemical interactions, and biological roles of small natural molecules in plants and fungi, with an emphasis on specialized metabolites, chemical mediators, and relevant molecular networks of functional gene and protein regulation (https://www.ipb-halle.de/en/).Dr. Clemence MarchalResearch AssociateTelefon: 0345 55821440clemence.marchal@ipb-halle.deLeibniz-Institut für Pflanzenbiochemie (IPB)Weinberg 306120 Halle (Saale)

jobs.description: Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany’s largest universities and a leader in research and medical training. With around 30,000 students and more than 5000 members of staff across 14 faculties, it is at the heart of the vibrant and outward-looking city of Leipzig. Leipzig University offers an innovative and international working environment as well as an exciting range of career opportunities in research, teaching, knowledge and technology transfer, infrastructure and administration.The Institute for Geography at the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences seeks to fill the above position.The PhD position is part of the project “CASCADE – Cascading impacts of climate extremes: new perspectives for interlinking Earth System Sciences in Leipzig” on compound and cascading impacts of climate extremes. CASCADE investigates how floods and droughts affect society and the environment, combining large-scale data analysis with a systems perspective on human–environment interactions.Our knowledge of the impacts of climate extremes is only as good as the data that record them. The PhD project aims to uncover biases in climate impact databases and research and to provide a more comprehensive view of flood and drought impacts at the global scale. To this end, the doctoral researcher will link and harmonise existing databases (e.g. ROUGE, Wikimpacts, EM-DAT) into a common event, impact and spatial framework, and will contribute to developing a multilingual news-based impact dataset that helps to fill gaps in existing sources. Using independent global hazard and exposure data as a reference, the project will analyse where and for which impacts the sources agree, how reported magnitudes differ, and how the likelihood that an event is recorded at all depends on hazard severity, exposure, socioeconomic conditions, language and media presence.The project benefits from close collaboration with the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ). The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team at the interface of geography, climate-risk research and data science.About the position- Salary group 13  TV-L - Fixed term of 3 years, Qualification-related purposes - 75 % of a full-time position, part-time employment possible- Start date: 1 March 2027The role- Linking and harmonisation of text-based and established impact databases (e.g. ROUGE, Wikimpacts, news-based data, EM-DAT) into a common global event, impact and spatial framework- Comparative analysis of where, when and for which impact types the datasets converge or diverge, using global hazard and exposure data as an independent reference- Analysis of the geographical, socioeconomic and linguistic factors that shape the visibility of impacts in different data sources- Development of a combined, bias-aware global view of flood and drought impacts- Contribution to the development and validation of a multilingual news-based impact dataset using natural language processing (NLP) and large language models (LLMs)- Publication of results in international peer-reviewed journals, presentation at scientific conferences and open publication of code and dataAbout you- University degree (e.g. master’s) or equivalent in geography, computational social sciences, digital humanities, environmental or earth system sciences, disaster risk research or a closely related field- Experience in data analysis, in particular in combining and harmonising heterogeneous datasets, e.g. demonstrated through the master’s thesis, research projects or work experience- Excellent programming skills (e.g. Python, R)- Experience in the analysis of spatial data, e.g. spatial statistics- Interest in climate-risk, natural-hazard or disaster research, e.g. demonstrated through coursework or the master’s thesis- Very good written and spoken English (at least language proficiency level B2)- Experience with, or demonstrable interest in, natural language processing or large language models preferable, e.g. through coursework or projectsWhat we offer you- a varied role with a high degree of responsibility in the dynamic environment of a major university- Collaboration in a friendly, supportive and motivated team- flexible working hours and mobile working to support work-life balance- Goal-oriented staff development throughout your working life, with opportunities for continuing professional development- a wide range of occupational health management services - Remuneration in line with the collective bargaining agreement of the federal states (TV-L), including an annual special payment and occupational pension scheme- excellent transport links and the option to purchase a discounted public transport ticket, such as the Deutschlandticket as a commuter pass- a wide range of food options in the refectories and cafés operated by Studentenwerk Leipzig.Leipzig University aims to increase the proportion of women in positions of responsibility and therefore expressly invites qualified women to apply. Severely disabled persons – or persons deemed legally equal to them under Book IX of the German Social Code – are encouraged to apply and will be given preference in the case of equal suitability. Materials used in the machine can degrade over time, simple factors like –outside temperature can fluctuate, and high usage and low usage play a roll. For stable process results, specific machine settings and recipe parameters are tuned automatically or manually. You already have a scientist´s or an engineer´s view. You know and see the parameters available, regardless of current usage. jobs.description: Weitere Berufsbezeichnung:Technische Informatik; Software-Engineering; Künstliche Intelligenz; InformationswissenschaftStellenbeschreibung:As part of the German government's artificial intelligence (AI) strategy, the successful Saxon competence center ScaDS.AI Dresden/Leipzig (Center for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence) is being expanded into a leading German AI competence center for Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI). For TUD Dresden University of Technology, diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.At the Center for Interdisciplinary Digital Sciences (CIDS), the Department for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (ScaDS.AI Dresden) offers, subject to the availability of resources, two project positions funded by the BMFTR asResearch Associate / PostDoc (m/f/x)(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)starting as soon as possible. The positions are fixed-term until March 31, 2029. The individual contract duration will be determined according to the candidate’s qualifications and the intended academic qualification goal. An extension may be possible subject to the availability of resources. The period of employment is governed by § 2 (2) Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG). A shorter contract term is possible by arrangement. Within the project Neuro-Symbolic AI with Logic-Memory Decomposition (Neuro-SAIL), a new class of architectures for verifiable neuro-symbolic AI is being researched using Logic-Memory Decomposition. Rule-based decisions are made by logic components, while memory modules are only used when information is incomplete or ambiguous. If no reliable decision is possible, escalation to humans occurs. The aim is to make rule-based decisions more transparent and efficient, to limit the use of neural models to necessary cases, and to reduce rule violations and unsubstantiated statements.Professional assignment: Chair of Scalable Software Architectures for Data Analytics (Prof. Dr. Michael Färber)Research areas: Natural Language Processing, Large Language Models, Knowledge Graphs, and related fields (e.g., Graph Machine Learning)Tasks: - scientific research and development activities in at least one of the above-mentioned research areas- participation in national and international research projects, possibly in collaboration with industry- preparation of publications in internationally renowned journals and presentation of research findings at conferencesRequirements: - a university degree (M.Sc., M.Eng. or equivalent) and if applicable a PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Intelligent Systems, Data Science, Computational Science, Mathematics, Applied Statistics, Information Science, Information Systems, Information Systems Engineering, Electronic Information Engineering, Computational Linguistics, Digital Humanities, Linguistics, or a related field- a strong interest in fundamental research in the above-mentioned fields- strong programming skills, preferably in Python, including experience with deep learning frameworks (e.g. PyTorch, TensorFlow) and related tools- good written and spoken English- strong analytical and problem-solving skills- high level of motivation and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team- research experience (publications, theses, projects) in the above-mentioned research areas is a major advantageWe offer:The position comes with access to high-performance computing resources and access to training opportunities within ScaDS.AI.TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. jobs.occupation: Research associate (m/f/x) for the CRC 1844 "Episodic Memory", Subproject A16 (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.87 hours/week = 75%) 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for oneResearch associate (m/f/x) for the CRC 1844 "Episodic Memory", Subproject A16The Department of Predictive Cognition is a newly established research unit within the Faculty of Psychology. After the completion of the new THINK research building on the former Opel site Mark 51°7, the team will move there https://www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/think/index.html.en. The research focus of our department is on combining neuroimaging and behavioural measurements with computational models to understand how the human brain learns and uses prior expectations during cognition. More information can be found here: https://blanklab.eu/The position is part of the Collaborative Research Center “Episodic Memory” (CRC 1844), an interdisciplinary consortium consisting of researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy, and neuroscience. The basis for our research is the Scenario Construction Framework, which conceptualizes episodic memory as mental simulations of past episodes, constructed from episodic memory traces and semantic information. As a part of this team, you will be trained in interdisciplinary research and have access to a broad spectrum of initiatives to support you in your academic journey. When we communicate with others, our perception of their speech is continuously guided by the memory of our past interactions. But how? In this CRC subproject A16 " Integration of episodic traces and semantic other-person models in a social context", we will investigate how memory traces of previously heard dialogues and the other-person model, which contains general semantic knowledge about the person, modify speech perception. This project places the generative model of scenario construction within a social context. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigate how EM traces and other-person models differentially influence the neural representation of speech and language.
